notes: [airpocket-01 = THE AIR-POCKET DIG STEP inside the drowning rescue (underground-safety phase 2 canary 1; OWNER approved 10-07 ~19:45Z). Variant for fleet 92bc84f: branch ap-on-92bc84f @ dbb4d78. Design docs/reports/airpocket-design-2026-10-07.md; evidence docs/reports/underground-safety-phase2-2026-10-07.md. NOT launched, NOT chained.] THE CHANGE (bots/src/airpocket.mjs + reflex.mjs wiring): a capped drowning rescue (route not `up`; at once when SEALED, else after 8 s) plans the first non-water cell within 2 of the head: a solid, non-falling, diggable roof cell with no liquid/falling/unknown on its sides or above (a dug cell above a submerged head stays air -- Paper sandbox2 10-07), or plain ice with air above (AP_ICE_ENABLED). Admission: predictedDigMs(fastest tool) x1.5 + 3 s <= (health - 4) / envelope, envelope 0.5 HP/s on peaceful without Hunger, else 2.0 (the pre-empt of an in-flight escape prices the worst case, floating). The dig is sent inside the step or never (bounded look, digGate, forceLook 'ignore'); a standing bot digs with jump released, a floating one with it held; a 250-ms watch aborts on > 7 HP lost in 10 s or the budget; success = eye in air 2 s AND health rising or at max. After success the bot STANDS with its eye in the pocket: 1-3 non-interactive-referenced scaffold blocks placed under it (floor, or a side wall with non-falling blocks only), each read back; escapes wait 10 s. The tick returns at the top while it runs; success or an opened pocket clears the rescue's fail memory. Rows only this build writes: _air_pocket_start, _air_pocket, _air_pocket_refused, _air_pocket_preempt.

licence.note: Written only by this build, one row per attempt (and _air_pocket_refused per refusal, throttled). The fleet build has neither.

draw_exposure.note: Each drawn pool must have REAL sealed drownings (air out: the oxygen filter drops stuck full-oxygen bots, e.g. placebo-b's 27 ceilings at oxygen 20). On 10-07 13-20Z: hive-c, hive-d, hive-b, placebo-a, placebo-d qualify. CLAUDE.md: a canary pool must contain the population the fix targets.

exposure.note: Ready = >= 2 MATURE canary attempts (start+end rows, 120-s follow-up inside the window) AND both control instruments visible (capped rescues >= 1, no-air sealed ceilings >= 1). Expected ~2-6 attempts per 6 h on pools that pass draw_exposure (dry run: hive-c+hive-d 16 no-air ceilings in ~60 bot-h), ~1 on average pools.

own_lines.note: C1: a canary _air_pocket success followed by the same bot's DROWNING death within 120 s.
C2: a lava/fire or suffocation death, or a lava danger-block row, within 30 s after any canary _air_pocket row.
C3: an attempt that did not succeed ending below 3 HP, or ANY death between its _air_pocket_start and _air_pocket rows (the 4 HP reserve must survive an abort).
C4: an attempt whose trigger_route is up (the swim was working).
C5: envelope 0.5 on a world that is not peaceful.

C0: an _air_pocket row with a missing/non-finite required field or no start row, or a start row with no end row while the bot kept logging for 120 s (unfinished). The gates above would read such rows as clean.
POSITIVE CONTROL: the control's no-air sealed ceilings (oxygen <= 0) are visible. BLOCKS KEEP.
A KEEP needs >= 1 canary success: attempts that never work are INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass. BLOCKS KEEP (INCONCLUSIVE).
POSITIVE CONTROL: the control's capped rescues (_drowning_route sealed/unscanned/out) are visible. BLOCKS KEEP.

primary.note: REPORTED, NOT GATED: attempts by outcome/kind, refusal reasons, predicted vs actual dig ms; DiDs of capped rescues, no-air ceilings, drowning deaths, all deaths, entombed+marooned rows and mine rows per bot-h; drowning deaths per capped rescue. POWER: no death endpoint is readable at 10 bots x 6 h (~0.8 drownings expected); the effect rests on the Paper sandbox scenes and the per-attempt gates.

harm.note: The death gate (two-death floor, OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control, from immobiledid, with the ADAPTIVE rule (OWNER 10-07): a trip with zero mechanism-linked deaths (linkage_extra) extends to 24 h on 20 bots under the three-part rule instead of an automatic revert. LAUNCH PRECONDITION: that extension tooling exists. The cross-sectional gate is biased for this draw: draw_exposure picks pools that drown more, and the base build on hive-c+hive-d in the dry run had 4 deaths at 0.067/bot-h vs control 0.021 (3.2x) -- a no-change canary drawn this way would trip on its own baseline.

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions. Bots dig roof cells and place 1-3 scaffold blocks in survival; no admin world state is created.

extension.note: Short canary for a fix-shaped change (owner 2026-09-29).

link_rules.note: a death DURING the step (no end row of the same id before it): C3

a death within 120 s after an attempt is linked, EXCEPT a drowning after an aborted/failed/opened attempt that ended at >= 3 HP (the reserve held -- the read's C3 is clean -- the base-rate drowning the fix could not prevent); after a success/opened, after an attempt that spent the reserve, or any non-drowning death, it is linked
a death after the step pre-empted an escape and no step followed: the pre-empt itself

underground_safety.note: Gate v34 (docs/reports/usafe-death-gate-2026-10-08.md): the death gate is a DiD of death rates, each arm against its own 24-h PRE, at the calibrated threshold in usaferule.py, because this canary is DRAWN on the pools that drown. Mechanism linkage by link_rules (usaferule.link_reason); any linked death reverts at the two-death floor. This replaces the former linkage_extra entry, a dict that crashed verdict.py and changerowcheck.py (both build a set from it).
